part2.intro: Three young people talk about their creative hobbies.
part2.question: For each question, choose the correct answer.

texts.label: A
texts.title: Ivan
texts.text: I've been interested in photography since I was ten, when my uncle gave me his old camera. I mostly take pictures of birds and wild animals, so I often have to wait for hours without moving. Last year one of my photographs was in a nature magazine, and they paid me fifty pounds for it! I'm saving the money for a better camera.

texts.label: B
texts.title: Chloe
texts.text: I write short stories, usually adventures with dragons and pirates. I write in the evenings on my laptop, and my best friend reads everything first and tells me what's wrong. She's always honest! My favourite writer came to our school last month, and I asked her for some advice. She told me to read as much as I can, so now I go to the library every week.

texts.label: C
texts.title: Raj
texts.text: I draw cartoons about my family – especially my little sister and our crazy dog. I started during the summer holidays when I was bored. I put a new cartoon online every Saturday, and now more than two thousand people look at them! My mum didn't like them at first because she's in some of them, but now she laughs more than anyone. One day I want to make cartoon films.

part3.title: The teenage newsreader
part3.text:
Every Thursday at five o'clock, thousands of children in Bristol turn on their radios to hear fourteen-year-old Zara Ahmed read the news. Zara presents Kids' News, a fifteen-minute programme on a local radio station.

It all started when Zara's class visited the radio station on a school trip last year. "The people who worked there asked if anyone wanted to try reading the news, and I put my hand up," she says. "I was so nervous that my voice was shaking! But the boss of the station liked it, and a week later she phoned my school."

Zara doesn't just read the news – she helps to write it too. On Mondays she meets two journalists from the station, and they choose the stories together. "We don't talk about the same things as the adult news," Zara explains. "Children want to know about new parks, sports results and what's happening at schools in the city."

Her favourite part of the job is interviewing people. "Last month I talked to a famous footballer. He was much shorter than I expected!" she laughs.

Zara says the job has helped her at school. "I'm much more confident now when I speak in front of my class."

Is she going to become a journalist? "Maybe," she says. "But I'd also love to be a doctor. I've got lots of time to decide."

items.q: How did Zara get her job?
options: She wrote a letter to the radio station.
She tried reading the news during a school visit.
Her teacher sent a recording of her to the station.

items.q: What does Zara do on Mondays?
options: She chooses news stories with other people.
She visits schools in the city.

items.q: What does Zara say about Kids' News?
options: It has different stories from the news for adults.
Lots of adults listen to it too.

items.q: What surprised Zara about the footballer?
How has the job helped Zara?
options: She feels better about speaking to groups.
She gets better marks in English.
She has decided what job to do in the future.

part4.title: The story of photography
part4.text:
Today, most people {19} photos every day with their phones, but photography is less than two hundred years old. The oldest photograph that still exists was made in France in about 1826 by a man called Nicéphore Niépce. It shows the view from his window, and the camera had to stay in the same place for many hours to {20} the picture.

For many years, cameras were big and heavy, and photography was very expensive. Only rich people could {21} for a photograph of their family. Then, in 1888, an American company called Kodak {22} a small camera on sale that anyone could use. People took their photos, then sent the whole camera back to the company. A few weeks later, they {23} their photographs and their camera back in the post.

Now we can look at our photos on a screen immediately and share them with friends {24} the world in seconds.

the boy hiding behind a tree and taking a photo of a fox

part7.model: One Sunday morning, David went to the park with his new camera. Suddenly he saw a fox near the lake. He hid behind a tree and took a photo of it. Later he sent the picture to the local newspaper. A week later, his photo was on the front page, and his family were very proud.

items.q: What does the girl want to be?

script.t: Do you still want to be an actor, Emma?
Not any more. I'm not very good at remembering my words.
What about a photographer? You take great pictures.
Thanks, but that's just a hobby. I want to be a journalist and write for a newspaper.

items.q: What is on TV at eight o'clock tonight?

script.t: Can I watch the quiz show tonight, Dad? It's on at eight.
No, it isn't. The news is on at eight.
Oh. When's the quiz show, then?
At half past seven, after the cartoons. So you can watch it before dinner.

items.q: What did the boy buy at the shop?

script.t: Did you get Grandad's newspaper?
Sorry, Mum, they'd sold them all. I went to two different shops.
So what's in your bag?
A magazine about football. I wanted to get a new CD too, but they were too expensive.

items.q: Which photo will the girl send to the competition?

script.t: Which photo are you sending to the competition? The one of your cat?
I can't. The rules say no animals.
What about the one of the beach at sunset? It's beautiful.
Yes, that's my favourite too. The one of my family is nice, but it's a bit dark. So I'll send the beach.

items.q: Where did the boy see the advertisement?

script.t: How did you hear about the new games shop?
I saw an advertisement for it.
On TV? I saw one there last night.
No, I don't watch much TV. It was on the side of a bus! It was huge.
Really? Mum heard about the shop on the radio.

part2.intro: You will hear a teacher telling his class about a visit to a TV studio.
part2.title: Visit to Bright TV Studios

items.label: Students will watch the filming of a ... programme

script.t: OK, everyone, listen carefully. I've got some information about our visit to Bright TV Studios. We were going to go on Tuesday, but the studio changed the date, so now it's on Wednesday. The coach will leave from the school car park at quarter past eight, so please arrive by eight o'clock. The journey takes about an hour. When we get there, we'll go on a tour of the studios, and then we'll watch them filming a programme. It isn't the news or a quiz show – it's a cooking programme for children, and some of you might get the chance to taste the food! The trip costs six pounds. The school is paying for the coach, so that's just for your lunch. You'll also meet the presenter of the programme, Lucy Dawson. That's D-A-W-S-O-N. She'll answer your questions about working in television, so think about what you'd like to ask her. And please don't bring cameras – you can't take photos inside the studio.

part3.intro: You will hear Lily talking to her grandfather about a school project.

items.q: What is Lily's project about?
options: how people got the news in the past

items.q: How did Grandad's family usually get the news when he was a boy?
What does Grandad say about the family's first TV?
options: Other people came to watch it.
It was a present from his father.

items.q: What was Grandad's job?
What will Lily do with Grandad's old articles?

script.t: Grandad, can you help me with my school project?
Of course. What's it about?
It's about how people found out the news when you were young. Our teacher wants us to talk to someone old. Sorry!
Ha! That's OK, I am old. Well, when I was a boy, we didn't have a television. We listened to the radio every evening. My father always listened to the news at six o'clock, and we all had to be quiet.
Didn't you read newspapers?
My father bought one on Sundays, but newspapers were expensive for us. The radio was the most important thing in the house.
When did you get a TV?
In 1965, when I was twelve. It was black and white, and the screen was tiny. But all our neighbours came to our house to watch it!
That's funny. Did you always want to work in the news?
Not at first. I wanted to be a photographer. But I got a job at a newspaper, and I was a journalist for forty years. I wrote about sport.
Wow. Have you got any of your old articles?
Yes, there's a box of them in the garage.
Can I use some of them? I could stick them on a big poster for my class.
Good idea. I'll find them this evening.

items.intro: You will hear two friends talking about a newspaper article.
items.q: What does the boy think about the article?

script.t: Did you read the article about our school in the local newspaper?
Yes. It says we've got the best football team in the city!
It's a nice article, isn't it?
Nice, but wrong! We lost every match last year. The journalist didn't check anything.

script.t: Hi Josh, it's Kyle. About the cinema tomorrow – I know we said we'd meet at two, but my mum needs me to help her at home. Can we meet at four instead? The film's on again at half past four. Oh, and bring back that DVD you borrowed, if you remember. Bye!

items.intro: You will hear a girl talking about a photography course.
items.q: What does she say about the course?
options: It was more difficult than she expected.

script.t: I've just finished a photography course at the art centre. I thought it would be easy – you just press a button, right? But there was so much to learn about light and colours, and my first photos were terrible! The course lasted six weeks, which was just right, and the teacher was really interesting. I'm glad I did it.

items.intro: You will hear a father talking to his daughter about a TV programme.
items.q: What does the father want his daughter to do?

script.t: Kim, that cartoon is so loud! I'm trying to work in the kitchen.
Sorry, Dad. Shall I turn it off? Or I can find something else.
No, you can watch it – it's Saturday. Just turn it down a bit, please.

items.intro: You will hear a boy talking about a film he saw.
items.q: What did he like best about the film?

script.t: I saw the new space adventure film at the cinema last night. The actors were OK, but nothing special. And some of the pictures of space looked a bit cheap. But the music! It was played by a real orchestra, and it was amazing. I've listened to it about ten times since then.

part5.intro: You will hear Josh talking to his mum about a media project at school. What is each person making?

script.t: So, Josh, how's the media project going? What's everyone making?
It's great, Mum. Ana's group is making a newspaper about our school. She's writing an article about the new sports hall.
Really? I thought Ana wanted to do a photo exhibition.
She takes some photos for the newspaper too, but the exhibition idea was too difficult.
And Pete? He's very good at drawing.
Yes, so he's making a cartoon about a dog who goes to school. It's really funny.
What about Hung?
Hung wanted to make a film, but he couldn't find a camera. So he's making a radio programme, with music and news. He's recording it on his laptop.
Clever boy. And Becky? Is she writing a song? She's got such a nice voice.
She sings a bit in it, but it isn't a song. It's an advertisement for the school concert. She wants everyone to buy tickets!
And you, Josh? You haven't told me.
I'm making a magazine about video games. Ten pages! I've already written four, and Pete is drawing the pictures for me.
